mappings.note: derives 1+2+...+n = n(n+1)/2 by the reverse-and-add argument - C-11.1-LO-1 word for word, and the only item in the chapter that derives a sum rather than a term
a and d recovered from two given AP terms, then the 31st term - LO-10's nth-term formula solved as a pair of equations
a three-term GP recovered from its sum and the sum of its squares; the work is entirely in the common ratio, so LO-11 - the tagged concept 'Sum of First n Natural Numbers' is wrong for this item
proves P^2 = (ab)^n from the GP nth-term formula (LO-11), and the proof turns on the exponents summing to n(n-1)/2, which is the first-n-naturals result of C-11.1-LO-1
three unknowns - a, r and n - all recovered from the GP nth-term formula; the heaviest LO-11 item in the chapter, and no sum is involved
counting multiples of 4 in a range is an AP term-position problem, solved with a_n = a + (n-1)d - LO-10; nothing is summed, unlike item 13
doubling bacteria is a GP with r = 2 (LO-11), and part (iii) asks for a general nth-hour rule, which is the explicit-formula deliverable of LO-8

part (i) asks for the sequence itself to be written out and continued (LO-7), parts (ii) and (iii) for an explicit rule and a term found directly from it (LO-8); the only item besides item 1 that reaches LO-7
one membership test that succeeds and one that fails on a non-integer n, both inside the AP nth-term formula of LO-10
a bouncing ball is a GP with a fractional ratio 0.6, so decay rather than the growth of item 32 (LO-11), and the marked deliverable is again an explicit nth-term rule (LO-8)
'increases uniformly by a fixed number every year' is the constant common difference of LO-10; every sub-part is the AP nth-term formula, forwards or backwards
concentric rows growing by a fixed 20 trees - again LO-10; part (iii)(a) even names the progression as an AP and asks for the 31st term
